secondary: Bell pepper and hot pepper (Capsicum spp.)

distribution: Worldwide; problematic east of the Rocky Mountains and midwest USA for tomato; common in potato-growing regions

tomato: Concentric 'bullseye' leaf spots on older leaves, brown to black, up to 1.3 cm
Yellowing or chlorosis around leaf spots
Stem lesions, dark and slightly sunken with concentric rings
Fruit rot at stem attachment points or through wounds, brown with dark concentric circles, black velvety spore mass
potato: Concentric dark brown spots on older leaves
Premature defoliation leading to tuber yield reduction
Tuber lesions: dry, dark, pressed into surface; underlying flesh dry, leathery and brown; may enlarge during storage

life_cycle.overwintering: Crop residues or wild solanaceous plants
life_cycle.infection: Conidia produced in spring, splashed or wind-dispersed, infect through wounds, stomata or direct penetration
life_cycle.spread: Conidia from lesions infect other parts of plant or neighboring plants during the same season

cultural_control: Clear infected debris to reduce inoculum
Water plants in the morning to minimize leaf wetness
Apply mulch to block soil splash
Rotate to non-solanaceous crops for at least three years
Control wild solanaceous plants near fields
Monitor fields closely in warm, damp weather
notes_on_resistance: Decreased sensitivity to QoI fungicides due to F129L amino acid substitution in A. solani
